fatal_errors: The proposed comparison changes both Co/Cr composition and annealing temperature, so it does not isolate a single intervention or distinguish compositional effects from heat-treatment effects.

The cited excerpt explicitly associates approximately 39.4 Oe coercivity with the Cr-substituted alloy annealed at 1000 °C, whereas the hypothesis predicts near 40 Oe after annealing at 600 °C; the supplied evidence does not establish that exact condition–outcome pairing.
explanation: This is a scientifically plausible alternative supported by relevant published evidence: Cr substitution and B2/BCC phase separation can reduce magnetization and increase domain-wall pinning and coercivity in AlCoFeNi-based HEAs. It does not reconstruct the target FeCoNiTi fcc/C14 intervention, phase chemistry, temperature-dependent transitions, or approximately 667 Oe coercivity at 400 K. Its baseline is also not well matched because composition and annealing temperature are changed together. TEM/XRD plus hysteresis measurements provide a reasonably clear test, but a factorial design separately varying Cr substitution and annealing temperature would be required to identify the causal intervention and mechanism.
